title: Migrating Toward Standalone APIs knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Migrating Toward Standalone APIs”?
options: Migrating Toward Standalone APIs helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Migrating Toward Standalone APIs means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Migrating Toward Standalone APIs removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Migrating Toward Standalone APIs should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Migrating Toward Standalone APIs helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Migrating Toward Standalone APIs is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Standalone component conversion” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Standalone component conversion” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Standalone component conversion” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Standalone component conversion” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Standalone component conversion” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Standalone component conversion” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Standalone component conversion” under Migrating Toward Standalone APIs. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Migrating Toward Standalone APIs”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
